questions.stem: What is the unit vector in the direction of the vector <3, 4>?
questions.solution: The unit vector in the direction of a given vector is found by dividing the vector by its magnitude. The magnitude of <3, 4> is sqrt(3^2 + 4^2) = 5. So, the unit vector is <3/5, 4/5>. Common mistake notes: Some students may forget to divide by the magnitude and instead use the original vector (choice B).
questions.explanation: Unit vectors have a magnitude of 1 and represent direction only.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Some students may forget to divide by the magnitude and instead use the original vector (choice B).

questions.stem: Find the unit vector in the direction of <0, -5>.
questions.solution: The unit vector in the direction of a given vector is found by dividing the vector by its magnitude. The magnitude of <0, -5> is 5. So, the unit vector is <0/-5, -5/5> = <0, -1>. Common mistake notes: Some students may forget to consider the negative sign when dividing (choice A).
questions.explanation: Unit vectors have a magnitude of 1 and represent direction only.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Some students may forget to consider the negative sign when dividing (choice A).

questions.stem: What is the unit vector in the direction of <5, -2>?
questions.solution: The unit vector in the direction of a given vector is found by dividing the vector by its magnitude. The magnitude of <5, -2> is sqrt(5^2 + (-2)^2) = √29. So, the unit vector is <-5/√29, 2/√29>. Common mistake notes: Some students may round the square root incorrectly or forget to divide both components (choice A).
questions.explanation: Unit vectors have a magnitude of 1 and represent direction only.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Some students may round the square root incorrectly or forget to divide both components (choice A).

questions.stem: Find the unit vector in the direction of <2, -3, 0>.
questions.solution: The unit vector in the direction of a given vector is found by dividing the vector by its magnitude. The magnitude of <2, -3, 0> is sqrt(2^2 + (-3)^2) = √13. So, the unit vector is <1/√13, -3/√13, 0>. Common mistake notes: Some students may forget to consider the third component, which is 0 (choice B and D).
questions.explanation: Unit vectors have a magnitude of 1 and represent direction only.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Some students may forget to consider the third component, which is 0 (choice B and D).

questions.stem: What is the unit vector in the direction of <-4, 3, -1>?
questions.solution: The unit vector in the direction of a given vector is found by dividing the vector by its magnitude. The magnitude of <-4, 3, -1> is sqrt((-4)^2 + 3^2 + (-1)^2) = √26. So, the unit vector is <-4/√26, 3/√26, -1/√26>. Common mistake notes: Some students may round the square root incorrectly or forget to divide all components (choice C).
questions.explanation: Unit vectors have a magnitude of 1 and represent direction only.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Some students may round the square root incorrectly or forget to divide all components (choice C).

questions.stem: Find the unit vector in the direction of <0, 0, 7>.
questions.solution: The unit vector in the direction of a given vector is found by dividing the vector by its magnitude. The magnitude of <0, 0, 7> is 7. So, the unit vector is <0/7, 0/7, 7/7> = <0, 0, 1>. Common mistake notes: Some students may forget that a zero component remains unchanged (choice A and B).
questions.explanation: Unit vectors have a magnitude of 1 and represent direction only.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Some students may forget that a zero component remains unchanged (choice A and B).

questions.stem: What is the unit vector in the direction of <-3, 0, 4>?
questions.solution: The unit vector in the direction of a given vector is found by dividing the vector by its magnitude. The magnitude of <-3, 0, 4> is sqrt((-3)^2 + 0^2 + 4^2) = 5. So, the unit vector is <-3/5, 0/5, 4/5>. Common mistake notes: Some students may forget to divide the negative component (choice C).
questions.explanation: Unit vectors have a magnitude of 1 and represent direction only.
questions.common_mistake_notes: Some students may forget to divide the negative component (choice C).
